alignments.note: Conditional particle to 'If'. SBLGNT.1CO.10.27.v023 is underdetermined over s001 with r00-base carried; the projection's reading is used as given under rule 12.
Substantival article before an adjective; the ASV supplies the pronoun 'them' and the case preposition 'of' rides with it under rules 21 and 22. Head on the nominal word 'them', not on 'of'.

The adjective is recast as a finite relative clause 'that believe not'; the relativizer and the negation are helpers on the word that carries the verbal content, as rules 31 and 32 place a relativizer on the clause's verb rather than on the substantivizing article.

'biddeth … to a feast': the italicized 'to a feast' completes the English expression of καλεῖ, which alone licenses it (rules 7 and 103's licensing test), and rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it added. Head on the verb word 'biddeth'.
Inflected verb takes its English subject and copular auxiliary under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical predicate 'disposed' rather than on 'ye' or 'are'.
No conjunction governs the clause, so the infinitival 'to' is rule 7's ordinary helper on its own verb (rule 61).
Universal quantifier compressed with the following substantival article into the single word 'whatsoever'; rule 80 gives that one word to the quantifier.

Substantival article before the participle: rule 32 allows it the pronoun and nothing else, and the quantifier has already taken the one English word the ASV wrote, so nothing is left for it (rule 80). A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement; that is not a correction.

Participle rendered as a finite passive 'is set'; the copula is the verb's own auxiliary under rule 9. Head on the verb word 'set'. The preverb's English particle does not stay inside this unit, because a source token stands to answer to it: rule 106 scopes the preverb-particle treatment to a particle no other source token answers to, and the bare dative ὑμῖν is such a token.

The compound verb governs a bare dative that the ASV writes with the English preposition 'before', which realizes the case government and rides with the governed word under rules 21, 36 and 106, exactly as ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς → 'came' and 'upon them' and ἐπέβαλον … αὐτοῖς → 'laid' and 'on them' do. Head on the pronoun. Reading 'before' as the preverb παρα-'s own particle inside the verb's unit is the competing analysis, but rule 106 settles it for a governed dative.

Participle to 'asking'. The competing reading takes 'asking … question' as a light-verb rendering headed on 'question' under rules 73 and 91; I take 'question' as the generic noun the ASV supplies for the negative indefinite instead, which leaves the participle its own ordinary verb word.
Negative indefinite carrying the clause's whole negation, expanded with a supplied generic noun; rule 17's generic-noun clause, as rule 69 heads οὐδένα → 'any man' on 'any', keeps the head on 'no'.
The discontinuous frame 'for … sake' wraps the phrase and stays whole on the expressed preposition, headed on the prepositional word (rules 78 and 46); rule 15 permits the discontinuity.
The ASV writes 'for conscience sake' with no determiner for the noun, so the article has no English 'the' to anchor and rule 21 forbids leaving a bare 'for' on it (rule 23).

review_notes: Corrected: 'before' (t022) moved from παρατιθέμενον to the governed dative ὑμῖν. Rule 106 scopes the preverb-particle treatment to a particle no other source token stands to answer to, and its closing clause gives the English preposition of a compound verb's bare dative to the governed word, as ACT.4.1 ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς → 'came' + 'upon them' and ACT.4.3 ἐπέβαλον … αὐτοῖς → 'laid' + 'on them' do.
All 19 source and 30 target IDs partitioned exactly once.
s011 and s018 remain the only unrepresented units; no added units, the italicized 'to a feast' being licensed by καλεῖ under rules 7, 11 and 103.
Other contested points left as flagged in their notes: the head of 'asking no question' and the placement of the supplied 'question'.
